description: Composite of three stacked binary phase diagrams for the Fe–C system with Mn or Al addition, all drawn on identical axes: y = Temperature, °C (200–1600, 200 °C ticks), x = C content, wt.% (0–4.0, 0.5 wt.% ticks). (a) Fe–C: fields labelled L, L+δ, δ, γ, L+γ, γ+M3C and α+M3C, with horizontal lines near 1200 °C and ~700 °C; the S point sits between the 0.5 and 1.0 wt.% C gridlines just above 700 °C and the E point between the 1.5 and 2.0 wt.% C gridlines just below the 1200 °C line. (b) Fe–15Mn–C: the γ field is pushed down, S moves to very low C (left of the 0.5 gridline) at about 600 °C, and the sub-solidus region is divided into α+γ, α+γ+M3C, α+M23C6, α+M7C3, α+M7C3+M23C6, α+M3C+M7C3 and α+M3C fields. (c) Fe–7Al–C: (γ+M3C) is replaced by γ+κ and γ+κ+M3C, new δ+γ, α(δ)+γ+κ, α+κ, α+κ+M3C and κ+B2 fields appear, and a dashed curve descends from ~500 °C at 0 wt.% C to ~200 °C near 2.2 wt.% C. The group argues that Mn expands/stabilises austenite to lower temperature, while Al destabilises it and promotes κ-carbide and B2 ordering.

observations.observation: All three panels are phase diagrams sharing the same axes: Temperature, °C (200–1600) versus C content, wt.% (0–4.0).
Panel (a), the plain Fe–C diagram, labels the fields L, L+δ, δ, γ, L+γ, γ+M3C and α+M3C, with S and E points marked and horizontal lines near 1200 °C and ~700 °C.
Panel (b) labels α+γ, α+γ+M3C, α+M23C6, α+M7C3, α+M7C3+M23C6, α+M3C+M7C3 and α+M3C fields in its lower region, and places the S point at very low C near 600 °C.

Panel (c) labels L+δ, δ, δ+γ, γ, L+γ, γ+κ, γ+κ+M3C, α(δ)+γ+κ, α+κ, α+κ+M3C and κ+B2 fields and contains a dashed curve that descends from about the 500 °C level at 0 wt.% C to roughly the 200 °C level near 2.2 wt.% C.
The γ single-phase region reaches markedly lower temperature and lower C content in (b) than in (a), whereas in (c) the γ field is truncated by γ+κ fields.
The caption states the dashed line in (c) indicates the A2 to B2 transition temperature caused by Al addition.
The caption identifies the three diagrams as the Fe–C, Fe–15Mn–C and Fe–7Al–C systems (written FeeC, Fee15MneC, Fee7AleC), compiled from refs. [31–35].
The citing text states that in the Fe–C diagram the primary phases are ferrite (α and δ), austenite (γ) and cementite (M3C, where M is Fe or Mn).
The citing text states that Mn addition promotes expansion of the austenite phase region to lower temperature.

The citing text defines the S-point as the lowest temperature at which austenite exists as a single phase, and states that below it γ-austenite decomposes into α-ferrite and carbide, even forming M7C3 and M23C6.
The citing text states that increasing Mn content decreases the C content and the S-point temperature, and that more than 20 wt.% Mn may accelerate formation of the β-Mn brittle phase.

The citing text states that Al addition replaces the (γ+M3C) region with (γ+κ) and (γ+κ+M3C) regions, and that as the S-point temperature and C content increase the (δ+γ) region expands while the γ single-phase region migrates to the right.

subfigures.description: Binary Fe–C phase diagram, Temperature 200–1600 °C vs C content 0–4.0 wt.%. Red-labelled fields: L, L+δ, δ, γ, L+γ, γ+M3C, α+M3C; S (eutectoid-type point) and E points marked, with horizontal reference lines near 1200 °C and ~700 °C.

Fe–15Mn–C phase diagram on the same axes. The γ single-phase field extends to much lower C and temperature; the S label lies at very low C just above the 600 °C line. The lower half is subdivided into α+γ, α+γ+M3C, α+M23C6, α+M7C3, α+M7C3+M23C6, α+M3C+M7C3 and α+M3C regions.

Fe–7Al–C phase diagram on the same axes. Fields L, L+δ, δ, δ+γ, γ, L+γ, γ+κ, γ+κ+M3C, α(δ)+γ+κ, α+κ, α+κ+M3C and κ+B2; S marked near 0.8–1.0 wt.% C at ~1050 °C. A dashed curve falls from ~500 °C at 0 wt.% C to ~200 °C at about 2.2 wt.% C.
